en.title: Dynamic Wall Building and Range Query
en.description:
Walls are built dynamically on one-dimensional positions indexed 0 to n−1. Initially there are no walls. build i builds a wall at position i, and building there again does not change the state; query l r asks whether the closed interval [l,r] contains at least one wall. This site's input convention: the first line is n q, followed by q lines, each a build i or a query l r. This site's supplementary ranges: 1≤n,q≤200000, all indices lie in 0..n−1, and queries satisfy l≤r.

The input protocol and the explicitly marked "this site's supplement" ranges were prepared by this site and are not extra conditions of the original problem.
en.input: The first line contains n q; then q lines of operations, build i or query l r.
en.output: Output 0 or 1 for each query in order, separated by spaces; 1 if the interval contains a wall, otherwise 0.
en.explanation: See the accompanying solution for the approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
hints: First pin down how each operation affects the state, then choose direct simulation or a data structure that supports range counting.
